editorial.headline: Technical Testing: The Discipline Behind a Valid Result
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers technical testing, calibration and laboratory work across materials, equipment, products and environmental indicators, with national PMA openness extending to Bali.
editorial.body:
Technical testing is the business of making materials, processes, products and instruments answerable to evidence. This activity includes sampling to establish the characteristics of a material or process; assessing physical characteristics, composition and performance; and operating laboratories on a periodic basis. Its remit is deliberately broad: testing may be physical, mechanical, chemical, biological, microbiological, electrical, nuclear-power-related, visual or checklist-based, forensic, or otherwise analytical. The work reaches across industry, trade, energy and mineral resources, construction, transport, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, food, agriculture, forestry and environmental measurement, including water, air and soil quality.

It also covers calibration and metrology across measurements such as temperature, mass, volume, pressure, force, torque, flow, hardness, density, length, electricity, magnetism, time, frequency, acoustics, vibration, photometry, radiometry and ionising-radiation analytical instruments. Industrial instruments, machinery and measuring equipment fall within that calibration work, as do periodic testing or calibration of medical equipment, electronics and other technologies. The scope further includes animal, plant and fisheries quarantine testing, marine testing, and work on ionising-radiation equipment including surveymeters, contamination meters, dosimeters and X-ray multimeters. Calibration may also include verification and stamping so that a measuring or calibration instrument can be regarded as valid.

Businesses may register at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. At the national level, PMA participation is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clean national position: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali’s position is also open in practical terms. The province’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and PMA registration is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; that higher-risk classification is specifically why this activity is not caught by the moratorium. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA restriction applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities, not to this one. For a technical-testing operator, the distinction matters: the activity is nationally open and remains registrable for PMA in Bali, while its risk position at the largest scale sits above the moratorium’s threshold.
